characters.name: Aulus Paulinus
characters.description: A Roman general. He got appointed as the governor of Britain in lieu of Marcus Sulpicius after being overheard insulting the Emperor's belovedPortia. Benevolent Boss: No matter how rude, stupid and incompetent his underlings are, Aulus never treats them badly. He also takes their suggestions to heart and has a lasseiz-faire approach to letting them do what they want. Brutal Honesty: He's very brutally honest about his negative opinion on people, such as insulting his Emperor for his attachment to his horse and admitting he doesn't care about Badvok when he's in danger because he's a bad person. The Conscience:Unlike the rest of the Romans, Aulus doesn't hate British people (he even falls for one, Gargamadua) and seeks to improve their lives when he becomes governor. He also shows disapproval when his friends and allies use foul language.In the episode when Badvok is kidnapped, we see two consciences of Aulus pop up; one encourages him to do the right thing and save him and the other encourages him to sleep with Badvok's girlfriend Gargamadua, who he likes. Guess which one he listens to. Though he does eventually send for his men to find Badvok. characters.name: Badvoc
characters.description: All Men Are Perverts: He develops an addiction to visiting a brothel in Romford despite being married to Gargamadua, and goes to extreme lengths to protect it from being taken down, including lying to Aulus that he'll anger some deities if he does so. Awful Wedded Life: Gargamadua may be dating Badvok, but she hates him and insults him on a regular basis because of his abhorrent personality. She even asks Aulus to hide her from him when he comes to the palace at one point. Badvok in turn often cheats on her and rarely spends time with her, preferring to lead his tribe of men instead. Bad Liar: When Gargamadua catches Badvoc cheating, he tries to claim he's just a random person with a similar appearance. He realizes she isn't buying it and allows her to hit him. Black Comedy Rape: When Badvok says that women are molested on a regular basis, Gargamadua notes how that happens only on the nights when he is out. Covered in Gunge: In the fifth episode of the first series Badvokis kidnapped and, in one scene, is tortured by being stuck in a barrel of...are you ready for this?human faeces. He's totally unfazed.

When Badvoc is kidnapped and Aulus sleeps with Gargamadua, he lies and says it was Grasentius who slept with her while he was gone, causing Badvoc to beat hom up. The Friend Nobody Likes: Emperor Hadrian hates him, rejecting his offer to stay with him in Rome and sending him off to Chelmsford with Aulus. Aulus hates him because he trusted Grasientus to keep his comments about Portia secret and he didn't, which caused his expulsion. Badvoc hates him because he's a Roman (and Aulus' supposed ally). The rest of the palace guards hate Grasientus for being aSlime Ballto the point that when Aulus orders his guards to arrest "that filthy piece of work (Badvoc)" they think he means Grasientus and arrest him instead. The Load: Invoked. Grasientus caused Aulus to get expelled by tattling about how Aulus insulting the Emperor's relationship with his horse, Portia. However, the Emperor also decreed that Grasientus was to be by Aulus' side as he doesn't like separating families. You can guess how thrilled Aulus is about that, and he treats him with disdain.

characters.name: Gargamadua
characters.description: Awful Wedded Life: She is Badvoc's girlfriend, but hates him because he is a crudeJerkassand even refers to him as a "wormshagger" in a telegram. Though she is sad when he is kidnapped, she has no problems cheating on him with Aulus. Deadpan Snarker: Badvoc tells Gargamadua that she should have been a man, because she is so strong. Her retort? That Badvok should try being one too. The Immodest Orgasm: She screams loudly and passionately when Aulus gives her an orgasm. Oblivious to Love: Until Aulus confessed it, she had no idea he was passionately in love with her. Put on a Bus: Gargamadua is only present in the 1st Series.

characters.name: Emperor Hadrian
characters.description: Berserk Button: Insulting his horse, Portia, is a surefire way to get yourself in trouble - Aulus found out the hard way. Bestiality Is Depraved: He is attracted to horses and goats. Decision Darts: In the final episode Emperor Hadrian uses this method to decide which part of The Roman Empire he should visit, inevitably settling on Britain, after several tries to hit the map with the arrow.
